reason: Examined current direct dependencies thm-weierstrass-p-normal-convergence-and-periodicity, lem-weierstrass-p-degree-two-and-half-periods, thm-elliptic-function-divisor-laws, thm-laurent-expansion-annulus, thm-identity-theorem-holomorphic-functions. Rechecked the quotient construction: projected straight segments make C/Λ path connected; the published path-connected-implies-connected theorem meets the Riemann-surface convention. First fix generic w with 2w∉Λ and ℘′(w)≠0. As a function of z the right side is elliptic. The degree-two fibre lemma shows denominator zeros occur only at z=±w; at z=w numerator also vanishes and the singularity is removable, while at z=−w Laurent expansion gives exactly the double principal part of ℘(z+w). At z=0 the z⁻² terms cancel and the finite limit equals ℘(w), fixing the remaining constant. Thus the two elliptic functions agree. The identity theorem in w extends through half-period and coincident-denominator cases, as an equality of meromorphic functions, without asserting a finite value at actual poles. Full source passages in Milne Ch. 3, McMullen Ch. 5 §5.1 and DLMF §23.2 were inspected.
